therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: HDL-C elevation via cholesterol ester transfer inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) or a CHD risk equivalent
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Absolute and percent change from baseline in HDL-C at Week 24

results.effect_size: Dalcetrapib: +12.76 mg/dL absolute change in HDL-C (+33.40%) vs Placebo: +0.50 mg/dL (+3.59%) at Week 24
results.target_engagement_evidence: CETP activity decreased by -56.5% (dalcetrapib) vs -5.69% (placebo) at 48 weeks; CETP mass increased by 86.45% (dalcetrapib) vs -4.93% (placebo) at 24 weeks
subgroup_findings: Mesenteric lymph nodes increased in volume: 4 (dalcetrapib) vs 11 (placebo) at 48 weeks
Mesenteric lymph nodes decreased in volume: 6 (dalcetrapib) vs 18 (placebo) at 48 weeks
safety_signals: Atrial fibrillation observed in 2/89 dalcetrapib patients (serious AE)
Various serious AEs including coronary artery disease, angina pectoris, glioma, metastatic squamous cell carcinoma, rectal cancer, non-cardiac chest pain in dalcetrapib arm
